battery.name: Battery Waste
battery.description: Batteries contain chemicals and metals that can harm the environment.
preparation: Do not open or crush batteries.
Keep damaged batteries away from heat and water.
Cover exposed terminals with non-conductive tape when appropriate.
recycling_methods: Take batteries to an authorized battery collection or recycling centre.
Use designated battery collection points.
battery.disposal: Never put batteries in ordinary household waste. Follow local hazardous waste collection rules.
reuse_ideas: Rechargeable batteries can be reused with compatible devices when safe and functional.
battery.environmental_impact: Improper battery disposal can release harmful substances and contaminate soil and water.
precautions: Never burn, puncture or dismantle batteries.
If a battery is swollen, leaking or hot, avoid handling it and seek specialist disposal advice.

biological.name: Biological Waste
biological.description: Biological waste includes food scraps, fruit peels and other biodegradable materials.
preparation: Separate biodegradable waste from plastic, glass and metal.
Remove non-compostable packaging.
recycling_methods: Compost suitable food and garden waste.
Use community composting or authorized organic waste processing.
biological.disposal: Place unsuitable organic waste in the designated biodegradable waste collection.
reuse_ideas: Use suitable compost to improve garden soil.
Use clean vegetable scraps for appropriate composting.
biological.environmental_impact: Composting reduces landfill waste and can return nutrients to soil.
precautions: Avoid adding plastic or chemicals to compost.
Follow local composting guidance for meat, dairy and oily food.

cardboard.name: Cardboard Waste
cardboard.description: Cardboard is a recyclable paper-based packaging material.
preparation: Remove plastic tape and other non-paper materials where possible.
Keep cardboard clean and dry.
Flatten boxes to save space.
recycling_methods: Send clean cardboard to a paper recycling facility.
Use designated dry-waste collection.
cardboard.disposal: Place clean and dry cardboard in the designated paper or dry-waste collection.
reuse_ideas: Reuse cardboard for craft projects and packaging.
cardboard.environmental_impact: Recycling cardboard reduces demand for virgin paper materials.
precautions: Do not mix heavily oil-soaked or food-contaminated cardboard with clean recyclables.

clothes.name: Clothing Waste
clothes.description: Clothing waste includes unwanted garments and textile materials.
preparation: Wash and dry wearable clothes before donation.
Separate reusable clothes from damaged textiles.
recycling_methods: Donate wearable clothes.
Use textile collection or recycling services where available.
clothes.disposal: Send unusable textiles to an appropriate textile collection service where available.
reuse_ideas: Turn old clothes into cleaning cloths.
Reuse fabric for bags, cushions or craft projects.
clothes.environmental_impact: Textile reuse and recycling reduce landfill waste and demand for new materials.
precautions: Do not donate wet, mouldy or heavily contaminated clothing.

glass.name: Glass Waste
glass.description: Glass bottles and jars can often be recycled into new glass products.
preparation: Empty bottles and jars.
Rinse off food residue when practical.
Keep broken glass safely contained and labelled.
recycling_methods: Use designated glass collection points.
Send accepted glass containers to glass recycling facilities.
glass.disposal: Follow local rules for glass collection. Do not place loose broken glass in ordinary recycling bins.
reuse_ideas: Reuse bottles for decoration where safe.
glass.environmental_impact: Glass recycling reduces the need for raw materials and can save energy.
precautions: Not all glass types, such as mirrors and heat-resistant glass, are accepted in bottle recycling.

metal.name: Metal Waste
metal.description: Metal waste includes aluminium cans, steel containers and other metal objects.
preparation: Separate metal from other materials.
Empty containers and remove food residue where practical.
Keep sharp edges protected.
recycling_methods: Send accepted metals to authorized scrap dealers or metal recycling facilities.
Use designated metal collection services.
metal.disposal: Follow local metal recycling and collection rules.
reuse_ideas: Reuse suitable metal containers for storage.
Repurpose safe metal objects for craft projects.
metal.environmental_impact: Metal recycling reduces mining demand and often saves energy.
precautions: Do not handle unidentified chemical containers.

paper.name: Paper Waste
paper.description: Paper waste includes newspapers, office paper and other recyclable paper products.
preparation: Keep paper clean and dry.
Remove plastic covers and other non-paper materials where possible.
recycling_methods: Send accepted paper to paper recycling facilities.
Use designated dry-waste collection.
paper.disposal: Place clean paper in the designated paper recycling collection.
reuse_ideas: Reuse one-sided paper for rough notes.
Use old newspapers for suitable packing and cleaning tasks.
paper.environmental_impact: Paper recycling reduces demand for virgin wood pulp.
precautions: Avoid mixing wet, greasy or heavily contaminated paper with clean paper recyclables.

plastic.name: Plastic Waste
plastic.description: Plastic waste includes bottles, containers, packaging and other plastic products.
preparation: Empty containers.
Rinse them when practical.
Separate different plastic types if local rules require it.
recycling_methods: Use designated plastic collection services.
Send accepted plastic to authorized recycling facilities.
plastic.disposal: Follow local plastic waste segregation and collection rules. Not all plastics are recyclable.
reuse_ideas: Reuse suitable containers when safe and intended for reuse.
plastic.environmental_impact: Plastic pollution can harm wildlife and persist in the environment.
precautions: Do not reuse chemical containers for food or drinking water.

shoes.name: Footwear Waste
shoes.description: Footwear waste includes old shoes, sandals and other footwear.
preparation: Clean and dry wearable footwear.
Separate reusable footwear from damaged items.
recycling_methods: Donate wearable footwear.
Use specialist footwear recycling programmes where available.
shoes.disposal: Follow local textile or footwear collection guidance for unusable shoes.
reuse_ideas: Donate footwear that is still safe and wearable.
shoes.environmental_impact: Repair, reuse and recycling can reduce footwear waste in landfills.
precautions: Do not donate footwear that is unsafe, badly damaged or contaminated.

trash.name: General Waste
trash.description: General waste includes materials that cannot currently be reused or recycled through available local services.
preparation: Check whether the material can be separated into recyclable categories.
Keep hazardous waste separate.
recycling_methods: Identify recyclable components before disposal.
Follow local municipal waste management guidance.
trash.disposal: Place remaining non-recyclable waste in the designated general waste collection.
reuse_ideas: Consider repair or repurposing before disposal when safe.
trash.environmental_impact: Reducing general waste helps lower landfill use and pollution.
precautions: Never mix batteries, chemicals, medical waste or other hazardous materials with ordinary household waste.
